The "Years of Lead"سنوات الرصاص in Morocco was a period of severe state repression, political violence, and human rights abuses under King Hassan II. Widespread arrests, arbitrary detentions, t0rture, and enforced disappearances targeted political dissidents, student activists, trade unionists, and the left-wing opposition. The era began to wind down in the 1990s with the release of political prisoners and subsequent institutional reforms. Yet the damage still remains till this day. Some people think because you deliver food you have to go along with anything. They see the job first. They forget there is a person behind it. Back home in Morocco respect comes before any request. Planning a trip to Morocco? 🇲🇦 SAVE this for later! Here are 7 things you should know before you go: 1️⃣ Haggling & Shopping — Don’t buy the first thing you see. Shop around, compare prices, and negotiate. 2️⃣ Tourist Pricing — Be mindful of how you identify yourself and where you’re from, as tourist prices can be higher. 3️⃣ Be Comfortable Saying NO — If you show interest in something, sellers may really try to make the sale. Be polite, but be firm. 4️⃣ Make Restaurant Reservations — Popular restaurants can book up, so reserve ahead of time if there’s somewhere you really want to visit. 5️⃣ Know How Taxis Work — Understand the pricing and meter system before getting in. 6️⃣ Explore Beyond Marrakech — You can experience a lot of Marrakech in 3–4 days, so use extra time to explore other parts of Morocco. 7️⃣ Agafay ≠ The Sahara — Agafay is beautiful, but it’s not the same as experiencing the iconic Sahara sand dunes. If you have the time, consider an overnight Sahara trip. Morocco is an incredible country, but knowing these things BEFORE you go can make your trip so much smoother. 🇲🇦✨ Save this for your Morocco trip and send it to your travel buddy! ✈️🐪 #traveltips #travelguide #travelcreator #moroccotravel #travelinspiration
